item.text: I’m reopening `SQLQueryCompletionItem` to collapse the remaining one-line factories into a smaller set of internal constructors/helpers. The goal here is to remove repeated instantiation patterns, not just rename them.

I’m going for the smallest refactor that truly centralizes construction: one private creation helper, then every factory routes through it. That removes the last ad hoc instantiation style without changing any public signatures or item types.
The factories are now routed through a single internal creator. I’m doing a final sanity check for formatting and any type-inference fallout from the generic helper before I stop.

`SQLQueryCompletionItem` now routes every factory method through a single internal creator, so the instantiation path is uniform instead of having each method directly `new` its item type.
